title: FA4 ignores `num_splits` on SM90 in v0.30.0 causing upto 48% slower decode
body: On H100 (SM90) vLLM v0.30.0's FA4 forward kernel ignores `num_splits`, so decode attention always runs as a single KV split. Models with few KV heads lose most of their decode attention parallelism. For [google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it) at ~6k context, a decode step is **48% slower** than on v0.26.0 at batch 1 and **36% slower** at batch 4. Results stay correct (the empty splits are weighted at zero) so nothing fails but it's just slow. The one-line fix was merged in the fork on 2026-09-28 as [vllm-project/flash-attention#198](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/198) (`6d11b3c`) but vLLM hasn't picked it up yet. The regression came in with the pin move in #54819: | vLLM | `vllm_flash_attn` pin | Has the fix? | |---|---|---| | v0.26.0 to v0.29.0 | `caaa4eb` ... `06bdd47` | Not needed, bug not present | | v0.30.0 | `506341a` (#54819) | **No** | | main | `9cd61de` | **No** (one commit behind `6d11b3c`) | **Ask:** bump the `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` to `6d11b3c` or later, and backport it to a v0.30.x patch release if there is one. The fix was validated at the kernel level and this issue adds end-to-end numbers on v0.30.0 below. We isolated it one component at a time on v0.30.0, starting from the end-to-end decode slowdown: | Step | What we changed | Result | Conclusion | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Split time to first token from per-token decode | Decode +48% per token, TTFT flat (61 ms on both) | Decode only | | 2 | Batch 4 → 1 | Gap *grows* (+36% → +48%) | Not batching or scheduler contention | | 3 | V1 v/s V2 model runner, text-only prompts, same MoE configs | V1 runner: +49% (bs 1), +34% (bs 4) | Not the runner, multimodal or MoE | | 4 | Context ~260 → ~5.9k tokens | v0.26 flat (4.34 → 4.38 ms), v0.30 +8% → +48% | Scales with KV length: attention | | 5 | `attention_backend=TRITON_ATTN` on v0.30 | Recovers ~70% of the gap | The problem is in FA4 | | 6 | torch.profiler per-kerne
label: bug

title: `draft_model` speculative decoding fails for Transformers-backend models: `ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`
body: `method="draft_model"` speculative decoding cannot start when the drafter and the target both run on the Transformers modeling backend. OLMo-2 is one example: since v0.26.0, vLLM serves `Olmo2ForCausalLM` through `TransformersForCausalLM`. Engine start-up fails with: **Minimal reproduction** On `main` (model runner V2, the default). Abridged: The V1 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) fails the same way, through `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py`. The failure does not depend on the drafter being the same model as the target. `allenai/OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct` as the target with `allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct` as the drafter fails with the same `ValueError: Duplicate layer name: 0.attn`. (For comparison, the existing test suite runs `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` as both target and drafter, and that works.) This is not #18503. That issue was a single-model OLMo-2 load failure from May 2025, fixed at the time, and it involved no speculative decoding. **Root cause** `Base._create_attention_instances` (`vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py`) names every attention layer `f"{i}.attn"`. It ignores the `prefix` that `Base.__init__` receives. The `draft_model` proposer builds the drafter in the same engine with `prefix="draft_model"`. That applies to both `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py` and the model runner V2 `draft_model/speculator.py`. As a result, target and drafter both register `0.attn`, `1.attn`, and so on, and `Attention.__init__` raises on the duplicate. Native models are not affected, because their attention names carry the full module path (`draft_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.attn`). **Affected** Any architecture that is served only through the Transformers backend (the `_TRANSFORMERS_SUPPORTED_MODELS` entries in the registry: OLMo, OLMo-2, OLMo-3, SmolLM3, Starcoder2, GPTBigCode, and others), when it is used as the drafter for a Transformers-backend target. I have a small fix and a regression test ready and will open a PR.
label: bug

title: ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch leaks stale state on unidirectional moves
body: On a `MoveDirectionality.UNIDIRECTIONAL` move `i1 -> i2`, `sync_batch` only clears the source index `i2`'s entry when the source index `i1` actually has state. If the request moving into `i2` has no `thinking_token_budget` but the slot `i2` still holds the state of the request that previously lived there, the stale entry survives. The new occupant of `i2` is then charged against the departed request's thinking budget and has `</think>` tokens forcibly injected into its output, even though it never requested a thinking budget. Reproducing the Bug Output: Fix Pop both endpoints unconditionally, matching `process_dict_updates`. This collapses the `SWAP` and `UNIDIRECTIONAL` branches:
label: bug

title: ThinkingBudgetStateHolder maps every request to logits row 0 when spec decoding is on but a step has no drafts
body: Summary `_apply_forcing_to_logits` derives each request's first logits row (`cu_num_tokens`) from `len(spec_token_ids[i])` whenever `in_spec_mode` is true and `predict_bonus_token` is false. On a step where no draft tokens were proposed, every `len(spec_token_ids[i])` is 0, so `cu_num_tokens[i] == 0` for *all* requests: the forced `</think>` tokens for every budgeted request are written into row 0. Request 0 gets other requests' end tokens injected into its output, and requests 1..n-1 have their thinking budget silently not enforced at all. Reproducing the Bug Output: Fix Only use the draft-token row layout when the step actually has drafts, and give no row to requests that own none (`_apply_forcing_to_logits` already skips `seq_idx not in self.cu_num_tokens`). With this patch both reproductions above behave correctly (`num_spec_tokens=3` matches `num_spec_tokens=0`; `cu_num_tokens == {1: 0}` with nothing boosted in the mixed case) and the property tests pass.
label: bug

title: DeepSeek-V4 VL dummy image is not the worst case for multimodal profiling
body: Summary `get_image_size_with_most_features` returns a square `756x756` image, but a square does *not* maximize the features within the token budget: real images produce up to **378 placeholder tokens vs. 346** and **3312 ViT patches vs. 2916** for the dummy. Memory profiling therefore runs on an input ~9% short on decoder multimodal tokens and ~14% short on ViT patches. Reproducing the Bug Fix Search the LLM grids that fit the token budget instead of assuming a square. The loop runs once at startup and returns `1932x336` for the shipped config, matching the sweep maxima for both patches and tokens. The `max_wh_ratio` guard keeps the returned size from being clamped back down by `load_image`; the selected grid also maximizes area, so it comfortably clears `vision_min_pixels` (649k pixels vs. the 147k minimum) and is not rescaled either.
label: bug

title: FilesystemResolver loads adapters outside VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR (path traversal via LoRA name)
body: Summary `FilesystemResolver.resolve_lora` builds the adapter path with a bare `os.path.join(self.lora_cache_dir, lora_name)` and never checks that the result stays inside the cache directory. A `lora_name` containing `..`, or an absolute path (which makes `os.path.join` discard the cache dir entirely), resolves to a directory anywhere on the server filesystem. `lora_name` is the client-supplied `model` field of an OpenAI API request (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/models/serving.py:304`), so the `VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR` confinement is trivially bypassable. Reproducing the Bug Fix Normalize the joined path and reject anything that does not remain under the cache directory.
label: bug

title: vllm.utils.system_utils.suppress_stdout silently suppresses stderr when sys.stdout is bound to fd 2
body: Summary The docstring states "Only suppresses stdout, not stderr, to preserve error messages", but the implementation redirects whatever fd `sys.stdout` happens to point at. Under the common `sys.stdout = sys.stderr` idiom, that fd is 2, so `suppress_stdout()` sends **stderr** to `/dev/null` — silently discarding error messages and tracebacks emitted by C libraries during `torch.distributed` group creation. Reproducing the Bug Run as `python repro.py 2> err.txt`; `err.txt` is empty. Target `STDOUT_FILENO` explicitly, so stderr is never a candidate.
label: bug

title: vllm.utils.system_utils.suppress_stdout crashes when sys.stdout has no file descriptor
body: Summary `suppress_stdout()` calls `sys.stdout.fileno()` unguarded, so it raises `io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno` whenever the application has replaced `sys.stdout` with a stream that has no underlying file descriptor — e.g. inside `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())` or in a Jupyter/IPython kernel (`ipykernel.iostream.OutStream`). Because `suppress_stdout()` sits on the core distributed-init path (`vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py:505`, `vllm/distributed/utils.py:556`), this aborts engine startup. Reproducing the Bug Fix Suppress `STDOUT_FILENO` directly instead of asking `sys.stdout` for an fd.
label: bug

title: AudioSpec(target_channels=1) does not produce 1D mono output for single-channel 2D audio
body: Summary `normalize_audio` documents that "For mono output (target_channels=1), returns 1D array/tensor", but single-channel 2D input — `(1, time)` from torchaudio/pyav, or `(time, 1)` from soundfile, both explicitly listed as supported input layouts — is returned as a 2D `(1, time)` array. Multi-channel input is correctly reduced to 1D, so the output rank silently depends on the input channel count. Downstream, `AudioProcessorItems.get_audio_length` (which uses `len(audio)`) then reports an audio length of `1` instead of the number of samples. Reproducing the Bug Output: Fix Squeeze the singleton channel axis when the target is mono and no reduction is needed. With this patch all shapes in the reproducer above return `(16000,)` / length `16000`, for both numpy arrays and torch tensors, and the multi-channel behaviour is unchanged.
label: bug

title: /derender logprob token strings drop SentencePiece leading space
body: Tokenizer only, so platform agnostic. Reporduced on `main` (741edeebeec3cedbe938d831b6d87641ed6191ef) with tokenizers 0.22. Logprob token strings from the derender endpoints lose the SentencePiece leading space. The engine path restores it (#48674) but derender doesn't. `resolve_token_id_placeholder` (`vllm/entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py`) does `convert_ids_to_tokens` → `convert_tokens_to_string([tok])` which strips the Metaspace `▁`. The engine uses `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` (`vllm/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py`) which puts it back. Same result with `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM`. - `/v1/completions/derender`: `top_logprobs` is `dict[str, float]`, so `▁true` and `true` collide and one alternative is silently dropped (the #48674 symptom). - `text_offset` is built from `len(token)`, so it drifts by one per leading space token. - Chat derender `token` / `bytes` don't match the coupled `/v1/chat/completions` output for the same token IDs. Resolve through `convert_ids_list_to_tokens(tokenizer, [token_id])[0]` so derender uses the same code as the engine. #58181 renames this function to `decode_token_id` and keeps the current body, so the fix fits best there or right after it merges. Related: #48674, #59046 (raised by @noooop), #58181, #47161.
label: bug

title: Non-streaming derender appends U+FFFD where the ordinary route emits nothing 🌈🌈
body: vLLM's scale-out token-in/token-out path (`/v1/chat/completions/render` to `/inference/v1/generate` to `/v1/chat/completions/derender`) promises "a fully formed `ChatCompletionResponse` without a GPU". When a generation stops in the middle of a multi-byte character, which `max_tokens` does routinely, the rebuilt response is not the same string: \n🌈' derendered : 'Output:\n Same request, same token ids, same `finish_reason`. The ordinary route holds the incomplete bytes back (they belong to a character the next token would have finished, and the generation ended first); the **non-streaming** derender decodes the whole id list in one call and gets a replacement character. The **streaming** derender in the same file does it correctly, it carries `prefix_offset`/`read_offset` through `detokenize_incrementally`, which is exactly the mechanism that holds a partial character across a boundary (as https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47161 describes). So this is not a judgement call about what to do with trailing incomplete bytes; one half of the feature already makes the other choice. At short lengths the difference is the whole answer: for `/v1/completions` at `max_tokens=1`, the ordinary route returns `''` and the derender returns `' �'`. **Versions** Reproduced identically on **0.27.1** and **0.29.0**. Stock wheels, one GPU, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, no special flags. **Reproduction** `repro_derender_replacement_char.py` go thru `max_tokens` 1…24 over three prompts, through three legs, and compares only rows where both paths emitted the **same token ids**, so batch numerics (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40896) cannot produce a false positive, seems like that one still in progress :) [repro_derender_replacement_char.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/5a260da5349fe424591f5b3c31c7733b#file-repro_derender_replacement_char-py) | arm | 0.27.1 | 0.29.0 | |---|---|---| | `/v1/chat/completions/derender`, non-streaming | **6 differing / 70 compared** | **6 / 70** |
label: bug

title: /scale_elastic_ep bypasses API-key authentication, accepts boolean counts, and returns 500 for unsupported scaling
body: `vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py` attaches the elastic-EP router inside `if "generate" in supported_tasks:` with **no condition on `--enable-elastic-ep`**. So `/scale_elastic_ep` and `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` are reachable on every ordinary vLLM deployment, including a plain single-GPU `vllm serve`. So there are few issues here With the server started as `--api-key SECRET-KEY-123` and **no** `Authorization` header sent: | route | status | |---|---| | `/v1/models` | **401** | | `/v1/completions` | **401** | | `/tokenize` | 200 | | **`/scale_elastic_ep`** | **200** | | `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` | 200 | The api-key middleware guards by path prefix (`entrypoints/serve/utils/server_utils.py:42`): `/scale_elastic_ep` is mounted at the root, so it is never checked. It is the only **state-changing** route in that position: `/health`, `/version`, `/metrics` and `/tokenize` are reads, while this one changes the serving topology and, while it runs, makes `ScalingMiddleware` answer **every** request on the server with 503. That is the part of this finding that matters. An operator who sets `--api-key` reasonably believes the server is closed; for this route the guarantee does not hold, and the impact is availability rather than one bad response. The two bugs below are what makes it reachable by accident as well as on purpose. In Python `bool` is a subclass of `int`, so `isinstance(True, int)` is `True` and `True <= 0` is `False`. The value passes, reaches `client.scale_elastic_ep(...)`, and the server answers: The request was **accepted and executed** on the same server, the same route, the same second, `{"new_data_parallel_size": 2}` returned 500. And the confirmation message renders the Python `bool` (`"Scaled to True data parallel engines"`), `True == 1`, so what was requested is "scale to a single engine". On a deployment running more than one, a JSON encoder that emits `true` where a count was meant asks for every other engine to be torn down, and is told it succeeded.
label: bug

title: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 is not batch-invariant for AWQ models on sm8x in the default mode
body: **Env** - vLLM 0.27.1 and 0.29.0 (pip wheels, same machine and same torch), torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.0; 0.29.0 reproduces this too - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (sm89), driver 580.126.09, single GPU, Linux 5.15 - model: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` (listed under "Tested Models" in docs/features/batch_invariance.md); `quantization=auto_awq` - controls: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (bf16), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a greedy request's output for an AWQ model changes when another request shares its batch. Unquantized and FP8 models are invariant under the same test; the AWQ model becomes invariant with `--enforce-eager`, and stays non-invariant with torch.compile on and CUDA graphs off, so the variance is introduced by inductor, not by CUDA graphs. title: v0.30.0: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash cannot boot on gfx942 — Engram pinned-host CPU offload lost on the AMD path (+47 GiB/rank GPU), OOM in profile_run
body: Serve command (production): Every startup on v0.30.0 dies in `profile_run` (~2.5 min into init) on all TP workers, and the server never becomes healthy: (The same model + same args start fine on the 0.29.x nightly image above the same GPUs.) Two facts combine: 1. **0.30.0 lost the Engram pinned-host CPU offload on the AMD/common path.** On the 0.29 nightly, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/common/engram.py:914` wired `cpu_offload=engram_config.cpu_offload if engram_config else True` into the `ParallelEngramEmbedding`, so the two DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Engram tables (94.4 GiB each; 23.60 GiB per rank at TP4) lived in pinned host memory and were read via UVA — each rank's log shows `Engram table offloaded to pinned host memory: 9600xxxx rows x 256, 23.60 GiB per rank`, and `Model loading took 100.09 GiB` per rank. In v0.30.0 the tree was renamed `deepseek_v4_1` → `deepseek_v41`. The NVIDIA path still reads the config (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/engram.py:358-365`, `get_current_vllm_config().engram_config`), but the AMD model instantiates the common `Engram` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py:64`), whose `ParallelEngramEmbedding._allocate_weights()` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py:695`) now allocates unconditionally on the current (CUDA) device — the `cpu_offload` wiring is gone from this path entirely. `EngramConfig.cpu_offload` still defaults to `envs.VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` = `True` in 0.30.0, and `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config()` even auto-creates the config for models with Engram layers — the AMD path just never consults it. title: Derender drops the leading space on SentencePiece tokenizers
body: Tokenizer only, so it's not platform specific. Reproduced on `main` (a2be4d3cc7) with `tokenizers` 0.22. On SentencePiece/Metaspace tokenizers, `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` drop the first output token's leading space. `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions` keep it. Thank you to @hyeongyun0916 for reporting it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-5857086699. The engine seeds its incremental detokenizer with the prompt (`DecodeStream(ids=prompt_token_ids)` for fast tokenizers, `convert_prompt_ids_to_tokens` for slow ones). Derender decodes the output IDs cold in every path in `vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py`. The batch paths call `tokenizer.decode` and streaming starts from an empty `DerenderStreamState`. The parser streaming path does this too, even though it already requires `prompt_token_ids`. A Metaspace decoder strips the `▁` from whatever token comes first, so without the prompt in front, the first output token loses its space. Tokenizer level repro (the same decode each path does): Against the render server: Derender should match the main path for the same prompt and output IDs (RFC #42729 / #47161). This hits Metaspace tokenizers with a dummy prefix: Llama-2, Phi-3/3.5 and older HF-format Mistral. Byte-level BPE (Llama-3, Qwen, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Phi-4) is fine which is why the parity test in #48617 doesn't catch it because it only runs `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`. I haven't checked `mistral-common` tokenizers. Parsers on the derender path also get slightly different input text than chat serving gives them. **Proposed fix:** seed derender's detok state from the prompt tail the same way the engine does and route the batch paths through `_detokenize_delta` so batch and streaming share one decode (related to #57593). Prompt IDs come from an optional `prompt_token_ids` on each derender request, then from `GenerateResponse.prompt_token_ids`. If neither is present it falls back to the curr

title: MooncakeStoreConnector crashes EngineCore when a request is preempted by `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` and re-admitted in the next step
body: Reproduced on vLLM `main` @ `0376f81530` (source checkout, not pip-installed, so `vLLM Version` shows `N/A (dev)`), with CPU-only torch. The bug is in scheduler-side connector logic and doesn't depend on the GPU. `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` preempts every running request outside `schedule()`. It is called from `pause_generation(mode="keep")`, where `clear_cache=True` is the default, and from `sleep(level>=1, mode="keep")`. Because the preemption happens outside `schedule()`, the next `schedule()` re-admits those requests right away. The comment at `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:2789` says this is intended. The same `SchedulerOutput` then reports each request both as scheduled and in `preempted_req_ids`. `MooncakeStoreScheduler` handles this in the wrong order: 1. During `schedule()`, `update_state_after_alloc` rebuilds `_unfinished_requests[req_id]` (and `load_specs[req_id]` on a store hit). 2. `build_connector_meta` then processes `preempted_req_ids` and pops those entries (`mooncake/store/scheduler.py:226-231`). 3. The request is processed as scheduled, but its state is gone: - V2 model runner, request in `scheduled_new_reqs`: `assert request.req_id in self._unfinished_requests` fails at `scheduler.py:245` - V1 model runner, request in `resumed_req_ids` (any role except a pure `kv_consumer` without `save_decode_cache`): `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` at `scheduler.py:298` - Async load (`load_async=True`, the default) after a reset without `reset_connector`, e.g. `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(True)`: the fresh load spec is dropped, no load is issued, and the request waits in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever The first two raise inside `schedule()` and kill EngineCore. The `reset_store` docstring names RL weight-update workflows as the intended caller, so `pause_generation(mode="keep")` followed by `resume_generation()` is an expected path. **Minimal repro**: Output: With `use_v2_model_runner=False`:

title: validate_xgrammar_grammar skips unsupported-feature checks for JSON schemas nested in structural tags
body: `validate_xgrammar_grammar()` does not check JSON schemas nested inside a structural tag for features xgrammar does not support, so those constraints are silently dropped. For plain `json` constraints, `has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features()` rejects schemas that xgrammar would compile incorrectly (e.g. `multipleOf`, which xgrammar ignores with only a log warning). With the default `backend="auto"`, that rejection is what triggers the fallback to guidance/outlines. The `structural_tag` branch only tries to compile the tag, so any `json_schema` inside it skips this check: validation passes, the request stays on xgrammar, and the output can violate the schema. A schema ends up inside a structural tag in at least three ways, all reproduced below with `{"type": "number", "multipleOf": 0.5}`, where the compiled grammar accepts `0.3`: 1. A user-supplied `structural_tag` (`response_format` or `structured_outputs`), in both the new (`format`) and legacy (`structures`/`triggers`) shapes. 2. Parameter schemas of strict tools, for any `tool_choice` that builds a tool-call tag (`required`, `auto`, named). 3. Harmony (gpt-oss), which wraps every `response_format` / `structured_outputs` constraint into a structural tag, even without tools. The same schema passed as plain `json` is rejected, as expected. Reproduced on `main` at `2b9b55c7f1` with xgrammar 0.2.7.
label: bug

title: rocm_unquantized_gemm crashes on CPU tensors (dispatch ignores tensor device)
body: `tests/models/language/generation/test_gemma.py::test_gemma4_dspark_loads_confidence_head` (added in #57263) fails on ROCm CI: `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py` picks `rocm_unquantized_gemm` for **any** ROCm build based solely on `current_platform.is_rocm()`, regardless of the input tensor's actual device: `rocm_unquantized_gemm`'s custom op is only registered for the CUDA/HIP dispatch key, so any CPU tensor crashes. The test builds `Gemma4DSparkForCausalLM` and calls `compute_confidence(hidden, markov)` with plain CPU tensors (no `.cuda()`), which routes through `DSparkConfidenceHead.proj` (a `ReplicatedLinear`) — on a ROCm build this always hits `rocm_unquantized_gemm`. The CUDA and CPU branches already fall back gracefully (`default_unquantized_gemm`/`cpu_unquantized_gemm` both ultimately call `torch.nn.functional.linear`), the ROCm branch didn't. Never caught before because this specific ROCm CI job (`amd-mi355-dpx-language-models-extended-generation`, `optional: true`) didn't run on #57263 itself. vllm-project/vllm#58867 (a different PR: AITER version bump) surfaced this while running full ROCm CI; fix proposed in #58923: guard `rocm_unquantized_gemm` with `if not x.is_cuda: return default_unquantized_gemm(...)`, mirroring the existing CUDA/CPU fallback behavior.
label: bug

title: Qwen3-Omni: M-RoPE positions silently misaligned for every multimodal request (offset double-counts the modality-start token)
body: Collected with `python vllm/collect_env.py` inside the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` image (vLLM 0.30.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12). GPU fields show "Could not collect" because the collection container was started without `--gpus`; the bug is model-side position bookkeeping and was reproduced with GPU access in the same image. `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration.get_mrope_input_positions` (`vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py`) misinterprets `PlaceholderRange.offset`: the prompt replacement machinery only replaces the pad token, so `offset` points at the first `<|image_pad|>` and the modality-start token (`<|vision_start|>` / `<|audio_start|>`) is already covered by the preceding text segment. The function instead treats `offset` as the modality-start index and emits an extra bos slot per media item, so the assembled M-RoPE positions are one slot longer than the actual token span. **Effects:** - With the stock chat template (text after the media item), the extra slot is silently absorbed by the trailing text: no error is raised, but every M-RoPE position from the first pad token onward is shifted by one — positions are wrong on all multimodal requests (image, audio, video). - With a chat template that ends the prompt on the media item, the consistency guard raises `RuntimeError: Position ids length mismatch with input ids length` and the request fails. The same off-by-one holds for the audio and video branches; audio-in-video shares the structure. **Minimal reproduction (no GPU or weights needed):** **Proposed fix:** PR #58890 drops the redundant bos slot and fixes the per-branch `st` advancement so the emitted position count always equals `seq_len`; the audio-in-video value structure is preserved, consistent with Qwen2.5-Omni behavior in HF.
label: bug

title: AITER v0.1.23 bump: gfx950 a16w4 MXFP4 MoE Gluon backend crashes (AttributeError get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout)
body: Bumping AITER to v0.1.23 (#58867) surfaced two upstream regressions, one already fixed in that PR and one filed upstream for tracking. ROCm/aiter#5259 removed the public `upcast_from_mxfp` helper with no replacement shipped in the pip package. Only used by `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, which had its own equivalent pure-PyTorch `mxfp4_dequantize` helper already — fixed by reusing that instead of the aiter import (already included in #58867). ROCm/aiter#5355 (in v0.1.23) added a Gluon-based `moe_gemm_a16w4` kernel for gfx950 and widened `_GLUON_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` to include it, so the default (`backend=None`) auto-detect on gfx950 now always routes to Gluon. That kernel calls `gl.amd.get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout(...)`, a Triton-Gluon AMD API only added upstream in triton-lang/triton#11470 (merged 2026-09-08) — newer than the Triton commit vLLM's ROCm images currently pin (`669b31a`, 2026-08-28) — causing: This hits `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp4_w4a16_moe.py`, i.e. any gfx950 (MI355) model using AITER's a16w4 MXFP4 MoE path (e.g. gpt-oss), not just tests. Filed upstream: ROCm/aiter#5888. **Workaround applied in #58867**: pass `backend="triton"` explicitly on gfx950 for both `moe_gemm_a16w4()` calls, forcing the known-good path until aiter guards its Gluon auto-detect against this Triton version gap (or vLLM's pinned Triton is updated past triton-lang/triton#11470). Filing this mainly for tracking/visibility — the fix is already in #58867. Will close once that PR merges, or if the aiter-side fix (ROCm/aiter#5888) lands and we want to revert the workaround.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DFlash speculator fails at startup (fp8_ds_mla draft KV dtype; 16384 vs 4096 hidden states)
body: vLLM `main` @ 73a78e6f1f, 2× B300 (SM100), TP2 + expert parallel. The backend check passes, and the profile run then fails: `aux_hidden_states` is empty here, so `propose` falls back to the target's final hidden states. For DeepSeek-V4 those are 16384 wide (4 hyper-connection streams × 4096), while the drafter's buffer is 4096 wide. It looks like DeepSeek-V4 doesn't expose aux hidden states for DFlash, similar to what #55682 adds for GLM-5.3-Flash. **Expected:** DeepSeek-V4-Flash + its DFlash speculator starts. Suggested fixes: pick a draft KV cache dtype the draft's backend supports instead of inheriting `fp8_ds_mla`, and capture the aux hidden states DFlash expects from DeepSeek-V4. For reference, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` (bundled DSpark drafter) starts fine on the same setup. Found while testing KV cache grouping for #58638. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to reproduce and write this up; I reviewed it.

title: When using the V4 parser in vLLM to parse outputs from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the leading extra space in V4.1 DSML tags breaks state machine matching and parameter regex, filters arg deltas, and prevents streaming return of tool call arguments.
body: vLLM does not ship a dedicated parser for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and reuses the existing V4 parser to process model outputs generated by V4.1 Flash. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash introduces an extra leading space inside DSML tags compared to the V4 specification. This difference triggers multiple failures in the legacy V4 parser: 1. The state machine for DSML tag matching fails to recognize tags due to the unexpected leading space. 2. The hardcoded regular expressions used in `_dsml_arg_converter` cannot match the parameter content, as the regex patterns do not account for the leading space. 3. The argument delta filtering logic with `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` buffers all delta content that does not contain the `>` character and suppresses incremental streaming delivery. As a combined result, tool call arguments cannot be streamed back to the caller. The proposed fix is to implement a new V4.1-specific parser inheriting from the V4 parser class: adjust tag definitions and regular expressions to accommodate the leading space, disable the arg delta filtering logic, and register the parser under an independent name.
label: bug

title: Responses API `truncation: "auto"` truncates at the token level from the left, dropping `instructions` first and cutting mid-item
body: vLLM `main` (also affects the pending Harmony fixes #38143 / #39413). The field exists but was a no-op in v0.15.1. `truncation: "auto"` on `/v1/responses` is implemented by mapping the request to `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`: - `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py` (main), inside `get_max_tokens(...)`: `truncate_prompt_tokens=(-1 if request.truncation != "disabled" else None)` — appears twice (initial request and the built-in-tools loop). - `-1` resolves to `max_model_len` in `vllm/entrypoints/utils.py::_validate_truncation_size`, and the prompt is then cut to the **last** N tokens of the fully rendered prompt (`SamplingParams.truncate_prompt_tokens` docstring: "will use only the last k tokens from the prompt (i.e., left truncation)"). That differs from the OpenAI spec this field is meant to mirror (`openai-python`, `response_create_params.py`): > `auto`: If the input to this Response exceeds the model's context window size, the model will truncate the response to fit the context window by **dropping items from the beginning of the conversation**. Two consequences of the current implementation: 1. **`instructions` is discarded first.** `instructions` is a top-level parameter, not an input item, so under the spec it is never dropped. In vLLM it is rendered as the system/developer message at the head of the token sequence, so it is the first thing a left cut removes. The model then answers with no instructions while the response object still reports `truncation: "auto"`. 2. **Truncation is not item-aligned.** The cut can land in the middle of a message, or in the middle of the chat-template header, leaving the model a prompt that starts with half a message and stray template tokens. Match the spec: drop whole items from the front of `input` until the rendered prompt fits `max_model_len - max_output_tokens`, keep `instructions` (and the final user item) intact, and never split an item. If a single item is itself too large to fit, return the existing 400 rather

title: Inconsistent merge/resolution semantics for flat and scoped `mm_processor_kwargs`
body: While investigating the two Qwen3-VL failures reported in #56363 and discussing the fix in #56372, we found that they expose a broader issue in the common `mm_processor_kwargs` handling: - vLLM accepts processor kwargs from both engine configuration and per-request overrides - and supports both legacy flat kwargs and Hugging Face modality-scoped kwargs such as `images_kwargs` and `videos_kwargs`. - For example, a video setting like `fps` can be provided either as a flat kwarg (`{"fps": 2}`) or under `videos_kwargs` (`{"videos_kwargs": {"fps": 2}}`). However, there is currently no single merge/resolution contract covering both dimensions. Depending on how the same effective settings are split across source (engine vs request) and scope (flat vs modality-scoped), values can be dropped, precedence can change, or flat/scoped representations can become conflicting again later in the processing path. The current common path first performs a shallow top-level merge of engine and request kwargs, then overlays a modality scope for vLLM-side reads. A single example shows the problem: The top-level merge replaces both nested mappings wholesale, and the subsequent video overlay replaces the remaining flat `size` mapping again. The effective video result is therefore: but the expected effective values are: This result follows from the two dimensions of precedence that need to be considered together: For example, request flat `longest_edge=1800` must override engine-scoped `longest_edge=1200`, while request-scoped `shortest_edge=200` must override engine flat `shortest_edge=100`. `fps=2` should remain because the request does not override it. So fixing only the shallow nested merge is not enough: the common handling also needs to preserve the relationship between source precedence and modality specificity. The resolved representation also needs to remain stable if it passes through another merge path. If an engine-level flat `size=X` has already been resolved to `videos_kwargs.si

title: Qwen2-VL video sampling divides by zero after rounding a one-frame clip to zero frames
body: `Qwen2VLVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample()` raises an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError` when a video contains exactly one decoded frame. Through the OpenAI-compatible API, this becomes an HTTP 500 response. The sampler rounds the available frame count down to a multiple of the default `temporal_patch_size=2`. For a one-frame video, that calculation produces `n=0`, but the function then uses `n` as a divisor. This report is specifically about the unhandled division by zero. Regardless of whether a one-frame video should be padded or rejected, it should not reach an internal arithmetic error. Start vLLM: Run the self-contained reproducer with [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563254/repro_qwen2vl.py): Observed output: `repro.py` sends two otherwise identical requests using embedded H.264 MP4 fixtures. The one-frame input fails, while the two-frame control succeeds. The server traceback ends at the frame-index calculation: Full log is here: [server_qwen2vl.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32563277/server_qwen2vl.log) The sampler should either: - produce a valid nonzero frame count, for example by repeating the single frame to satisfy the temporal patch size; or - reject the input with a clear validation error. It should not return HTTP 500 because of an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError`. For the failing input: `compute_frames_index_to_sample()` first rounds `max_frames` down to a multiple of `temporal_patch_size`: This makes `max_frames` zero. The subsequent clamp and alignment also produce `n=0`. The function does not validate that result before evaluating: The final expression therefore evaluates `1 / 0`. [#33746](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33746) discussed frame-count alignment for preprocessed Qwen3-VL inputs with `do_sample_frames=False`. The discussion favored an informative validation error when the caller supplies an unaligned frame count. That PR was closed without being merged and does not handle the one-fr

title: Realtime (streaming-input) sessions get ~3 ms slower per step for every minute   of audio — O(n) scheduler work in strip_covered_mm_data
body: With `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` on the Realtime API (`/v1/realtime`), the time per engine step grows linearly with the age of the session, with no plateau at the model's 8192-token sliding window. On our machine the median step goes from 26 ms to 59 ms over 12 minutes of audio, and p99 crosses the 80 ms real-time budget (one token per 80 ms of audio) at about 8 minutes, after which a single stream can no longer keep up. GPU utilisation *falls* while this happens. A py-spy profile of the EngineCore late in a session puts **~55 % of wall time in the scheduler**, in: A realtime session appends one multimodal feature per 80 ms audio chunk (750 per minute) and is re-submitted to the worker on every step, so `strip_covered_mm_data` walks **all** accumulated features on **every** step and builds a fresh `dataclasses.replace` copy of each one already covered, without keeping the result. ~4 µs × 750 features ≈ 3 ms of pure Python per step per minute of session age, which matches the measured slope (2.99 ms/min). Total work over a session is quadratic. `strip_covered_mm_data` came in with #52041. The decay reported in #39996 (0.19.x) suggests an older O(n) component existed as well; in 0.29.0 this function is the dominant one. - vLLM 0.29.0 (PyPI wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu132, transformers 5.17.0, mistral-common 1.11.7, Python 3.12 - RTX 3090, 4 vCPU of a Ryzen 7 2700 (Zen+). A slow core makes the effect large, but it is CPU-bound Python, so every host has it in proportion. One realtime session, all audio sent at once, so the spacing of `transcription.delta` events is the per-step cost (a ~60-line script using only `websockets`; happy to share it). Nothing else attached to the server. | session age (min of audio) | 0–1 | 2–3 | 4–5 | 5–6 | 6–7 | 7–8 | 8–9 | 9–10 | 10–11 | 11–12 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | step p50 (ms) | 26.4 | 31.7 | 37.2 | 40.0 | 43.2 | 46.0 | 48.9 | 52.1 | 55.1 | 58.9 | | step p95 (ms) | 28.4 | 34.0 | 41.9 | 45.8 | 52.8 | 6

title: CPU W4A16 Whisper fails: cpu_gemm_wna16 rejects 3-D encoder activations; packed k_proj bias is synthesized incorrectly
body: Loading a compressed-tensors **W4A16 Whisper** checkpoint on **CPU** (`CPUWNA16LinearKernel` / `cpu_gemm_wna16`) fails at runtime. The Whisper encoder feeds **3-D** activations `[B, T, D]` into quantized Linear layers, but the C++ kernel treats the input as 2-D `[M, K]` and reads `K` from `input.size(1)`. For encoder time `T=28` that is not a multiple of 32, so the kernel aborts. Separately, packed checkpoints expose `.k_proj.weight_packed` and omit `.k_proj.bias`. `_create_fake_bias_for_k_proj` only matches `.k_proj.weight` and sizes the fake bias from `weight.size(0)`, which is wrong for packed AWQ/Marlin layouts (`d_model` is required). After the crash is avoided, that produces garbage transcripts (WER 100 on LibriSpeech in our runs). Model: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized.w4a16 The request completes. BF16 openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo on the same CPU path is around 2.x WER on LibriSpeech; W4A16 should be in the same ballpark, not crash. - 3-D activations. ops.cpu_gemm_wna16 does not flatten leading dims the way int4_scaled_mm_cpu already does (x.reshape(-1, x_shape[-1]), then reshape the output back). Whisper encoder Linear layers therefore pass [B, T, D] straight into the C++ op. - Packed k_proj bias. WhisperForConditionalGeneration.load_weights only walks .k_proj.weight. Compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints use .k_proj.weight_packed and have no real .k_proj.bias. The fused qkv_proj/kv_proj path still needs a d_model-sized zeros bias; using packed dim0 is wrong. - Flatten/reshape in cpu_gemm_wna16 to match int4_scaled_mm_cpu. - In _create_fake_bias_for_k_proj, also match .k_proj.weight_packed, size the fake bias from config.d_model, and do not override a real .k_proj.bias.
label: bug

title: An Anthropic messages test is not compatible with Anthropic SDK 1.x
body: `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_messages.py::test_anthropic_streaming_cache_usage` passes `temperature=0.0` as a keyword argument to `AsyncMessages.create()`. That works on Anthropic Python SDK 0.x, but breaks on 1.x: This is a client-side SDK change, not a vLLM serving bug. Anthropic SDK 1.0 removed temperature / top_p / top_k from messages.create(), messages.stream(), and messages.parse(). Official migration notes: https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md#removed-deprecated-request-parameters Those sampling fields are gone from the method signature, not from the HTTP API. For older models that still honor them (including this test's served name claude-3-7-sonnet-latest), the documented replacement is extra_body: extra_body is merged into the JSON body by the SDK. vLLM already declares temperature on AnthropicMessagesRequest, so the server keeps parsing it as a normal field. No serving-side extra_body handling is required. vLLM depends on anthropic >= 0.71.0 (requirements/common.txt) with no <1 cap, so CI / downstream installs can resolve either 0.x or 1.x. extra_body exists on both generations, so this keeps the test working for both, but temperature= would get TypeError on 1.x. This test only asserts streaming prefix-cache usage (cache_read / cache_creation on message_delta). It does not inspect generated text, so it is indifferent to greedy vs default sampling. Dropping temperature entirely would also fix the TypeError This PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57780 keeps greedy via extra_body to stay closest to the original request.
label: bug

title: cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8 excludes SM89 (Ada Lovelace) despite native FP8 tensor core support
body: **Environment:** - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (SM 8.9) - vLLM: 0.29.0 - CUDA: 13.4 - Model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (block-quantized FP8, 128×128 blocks) **Description:** cutlass_block_fp8_supported() returns False on Ada Lovelace (SM89), causing block-quantized FP8 checkpoints to fall through the kernel priority list in _POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_KERNELS all the way to MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel — bypassing CUTLASS entirely, even though: Non-block FP8 CUTLASS is supported on this card: cutlass_fp8_supported() == True Ada Lovelace has native FP8 tensor core hardware, and vLLM's own docs state FP8 W8A8 is officially supported on "Hopper and Ada Lovelace" (https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/quantization/fp8/) Bisecting ops.cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_block_fp8() directly shows a hard floor at SM90: - 80 -> False - 86 -> False - 89 -> False - 90 -> True - 100 -> True **Question:** Is this a genuine CUTLASS-library-level limitation (e.g. block-scaled grouped GEMM requiring Hopper-specific TMA multicast at the collective-builder level, similar to the SM_120/SM_121 CUTLASS MoE gap in #43507), or is SM89 support for block-scaled CUTLASS GEMM simply not yet wired up in vLLM's compiled extension? If it's the latter, this is a meaningful gap for anyone running block-quantized FP8 checkpoints (increasingly common — DeepSeek-style 128×128 block scales) on Ada workstation cards (RTX 6000 Ada, L40S, RTX 4090), since it silently falls back to Marlin's weight-only dequant path rather than using the card's native FP8 compute. **Repro:**

title: New watermarking feature (v0.30.0) allows per-request opt-out even when server enforces --watermark-config
body: The watermarking feature was added in v0.30.0 (PR #54053, RFC #53916). This new feature allows per-request opt-out even when the server operator configured `--watermark-config`. A user can send `"watermarking": false` in a request, and the server disables the watermark for that request without any warning or log. This appears to be a gap in the initial implementation of the v0.30.0 watermarking feature. RFC #53916 states watermarking "is a modification of the sampling process, which cannot be modified by downstream consumers." The current implementation contradicts this — any API caller can modify the watermark behavior per-request. **Root cause:** `gpu_sampler.py` L41 reads `sampling_params.watermarking` directly. No code path checks the server's `--watermark-config` to override the per-request value. The `watermarking` field is exposed on all API endpoints: - `ChatCompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L270) - `CompletionRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L78) - `ResponsesRequest.watermarking` (protocol.py L217) **Steps to reproduce:** The outputs differ because watermarking changes the sampling distribution (Gumbel-max). The server accepted `watermarking=False` (HTTP 200) without error, even though `--watermark-config` was set. **Expected behavior:** When `--watermark-config` is active, one of: 1. Ignore the per-request `watermarking` field and always watermark 2. Reject `watermarking=False` with HTTP 400 3. Add a `--watermark-enforce` flag that prevents per-request opt-out **Why this matters:** The v0.30.0 watermarking feature was built for regulatory compliance (EU AI Act Article 50(2), California SB 942 — see RFC #53916). Without server-level enforcement, operators who deploy `--watermark-config` for compliance cannot guarantee all outputs are watermarked. Any API user can silently bypass the policy. The server logs no warning when watermarking is disabled per-request. Since this feature just shipped in v0.30.0, fixing the enforcement gap now avoids brea
label: bug

title: vLLM does not ignore temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty for DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, unlike the official DeepSeek API
body: Summary According to the official DeepSeek API documentation, the DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode does not support the temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty parameters. For backward compatibility, passing these parameters does not raise an error, but they have no effect. However, vLLM does not behave consistently with the DeepSeek API. When serving DeepSeek V4 series models in thinking mode, these parameters are still applied to sampling instead of being ignored. Expected behavior For DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode, vLLM should accept temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty without raising an error, but silently ignore them — matching the official DeepSeek API behavior. Actual behavior These parameters are still honored by the sampler, which can lead to different (and unexpected) outputs compared to the official API. Impact Users migrating from the official DeepSeek API to vLLM may get inconsistent results. Clients that rely on the documented "accepted but ignored" behavior may unintentionally change model output. Reproducibility across the official API and vLLM is broken for these models. Steps to reproduce Serve a DeepSeek V4 series model in thinking mode with vLLM. Send a request with different values of temperature (or presence_penalty / frequency_penalty). Observe that the output changes, whereas the official DeepSeek API would produce identical sampling behavior regardless of these values. Suggested fix Detect DeepSeek V4 series thinking mode and skip applying temperature, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty in the sampling path, while still accepting them in the request schema for compatibility.
label: bug

title: Mistral's "always adjust_request" grammar path rebuilds the tool parser and compiles regex over the full vocab on the main event loop, on every request — even tool_choice="none"
body: For Mistral models served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice`, every chat completion request — including plain-text ones with `tool_choice="none"` and no `tools`— triggers a full rebuild of `MistralToolParser` → `ParserEngine` → `StreamingParserEngine`, which compiles `regex` patterns over the tokenizer's entire special-token vocabulary (`_build_drop_info` in `vllm/parser/engine/streaming_parser_engine.py`). This runs **synchronously on the main asyncio event loop**, not inside the renderer's `ThreadPoolExecutor` (unlike tokenization itself, which is offloaded via `make_async`). Under concurrent load this becomes a bottleneck: the event loop can't advance anything else while blocked on it, so requests back up long before ever reaching the scheduler. Model: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603`, served with `--tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2` on 2×H200. Confirmed present, unchanged, in both v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 (checked directly against source). Root cause is `online_renderer.py`'s `preprocess_chat`: The comment above it explains this is intentional ("so that the grammar factory can prevent special-token leakage"), but the expensive part (`_build_drop_info`) depends only on the fixed tokenizer vocabulary/parser config — not on per-request `tools` or content — so it looks memoizable rather than needing reconstruction on every request. **Reproduction:** 1. Serve a Mistral model: `vllm serve mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral --tensor-parallel-size 2 ...` 2. title: Cross-encoder `padding="max_length"` produces incorrect `token_type_ids`
body: For a BERT-style cross encoder, `padding="max_length"` pads `input_ids` correctly but assigns every padding token the last real token's `token_type_id`. In a query/document pair that value is normally 1, so padding is incorrectly treated as part of the document segment instead of using the tokenizer's `pad_token_type_id` of 0. BERT consumes token-type embeddings, so accepted `/score` and `/rerank` requests can run on different segment IDs from the tokenizer's intended input. This can change scores, rank order, and threshold decisions. Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512913/repro_cross_encoder.py), run: The reproducer uses vLLM's released rerank request, tokenization parameters, post-tokenization logic, and worker-side token-type compression. An in-memory BERT tokenizer provides the Transformers reference result, so no model download or GPU is required. The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. Both paths produce the same padded input IDs: vLLM produces: Transformers uses the tokenizer's padding token type: Full log is here: [reproducer_cross_encoder.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32512950/reproducer_cross_encoder.log). `_apply_post_tokenization_to_token_type_ids()` pads with `token_type_ids[-1]` instead of `tokenizer.pad_token_type_id`. The following compression step stores only one zero-to-one boundary. That representation can encode `0*1*`, but not the correct right-padded shape `0*1*0*`, so the worker also reconstructs all padded positions as type 1. [PR #47772](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47772) fixes a different boundary problem after truncation. It does not change max-length padding or the single-boundary representation, so this case remains reproducible in vLLM 0.29.0.
label: bug

title: `/score` Unicode truncation can exceed per-input token limits
body: `/score` accepts `max_tokens_per_query` and `max_tokens_per_doc`, but the final query or document can still contain more tokens than the requested limit. This happens with ordinary CJK text and emoji ZWJ sequences. The request succeeds with HTTP 200, so this is not an unsupported configuration or a validation error. Callers cannot reliably enforce the documented per-query or per-document token budgets for multilingual input. Extra tokens consume context and compute and can change scores or downstream overlength behavior. title: Hunyuan A13B streaming leaks `</answer>` into `content`
body: The `hunyuan_a13b` reasoning parser returns different content for streaming and non-streaming Chat Completions when given the same well-formed model output: Non-streaming returns `reasoning="ink"` and `content="answer"`. Streaming returns the same reasoning but aggregates to `content="answer\n</answer>"`, exposing Hunyuan's closing framing marker to the client. Both requests succeed with HTTP 200 and contain exactly the same generated token IDs. Streaming clients receive model protocol syntax in the user-visible answer, while non-streaming clients receive clean content for the same tokens. Applications that render, persist, compare, or parse streamed answers can therefore expose the marker or produce mode-dependent results. The Hunyuan-A13B checkpoint is over 150 GiB and is not needed to reproduce a frontend parsing bug. The included debug logits processor forces the exact token sequence documented by `HunyuanA13BReasoningParser`, while the official Hunyuan tokenizer supplies the corresponding text. The requests still go through a real vLLM engine, HTTP server, Chat Completions serving code, and the production `hunyuan_a13b` parser. title: Partial cache events can reference unreported parent hashes
body: Hi, I believe I found a case where a BlockStored event for a partial block references a parent_block_hash that was never emitted. This prevents an external consumer from reconstructing the prefix chain. Consider a request having 1,800 tokens (so 1,536 + 128 + 128 + 8), and its tokens to be stored in a contiguous array `tokens`, and a Hashing function `H` (to simplify notation): The relevant chain is: `H1536 -> H1664 -> H1792` The problem is, we don’t emit a KV cache event for `H1664`. That is, an event is emitted only for the full block `H1536`, and for the final partial block hash `H1792`. However, we never received `H1664`, and we cannot decipher H1792’s position in the prefix chain without `H1664`. Our KV cache chain is thus irremediably broken. Code for full reproduction: Which produces: i.e., we get `H1792`, but its parent `H1664` was never emitted. PR #44488 provides a hint on fixing the issue, by introducing the `skipped_parent_block_hash` param in `BlockStored` events. I have an initial attempt [here](https://github.com/Lucas-Fernandes-Martins/vllm/compare/efc443a645f4986bc2f458d74ebf841e158a4813...1b2e19ed69) to use `skipped_parent_block_hash` to solve the issue, adding those fields to `cache_partial_block` by producing instead: Thank you very much and let me know if I can tackle this issue!

title: cancelling a background `/v1/responses` that already finished is refused with "Cannot cancel a synchronous response."
body: Only a correctness issue, doesn't affect performance, might just confuse people. `POST /v1/responses/{id}/cancel` refuses every response that is not `queued` or `in_progress` with one message, and that message names the wrong reason. A response created with `background: true` is asynchronous by construction, yet once it reaches a terminal state the API says it is synchronous: | response | `background` | status when cancelled | result | |---|---|---|---| | finished on its own | **true** | `completed` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` | | cancelled a moment earlier (that cancel returned 200 and `status: "cancelled"`) | **true** | `cancelled` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` | | control: an ordinary stored response | false | `incomplete` | 400 `"Cannot cancel a synchronous response."` — here the message is true | The second row is the funniest: the same endpoint cancelled that response successfully one call earlier, so the server itself already treated it as cancellable. `repro_responses_cancel_wrong_reason.py` (attached; stdlib only) runs the three cases above and exits 1 when a `background: true` response is refused as synchronous. It exits 2 if the store is not enabled, so a misconfigured server cannot look like this bug. `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py`, `cancel_responses`, one branch serves every non-cancellable state: `completed`, `failed`, `incomplete` and `cancelled` all land there, and so does the genuinely synchronous case. The message was written for the last one and inherited by the rest.
label: bug

title: `/v1/responses` output items are always `status: "completed"`, even inside an incomplete response
body: A Responses API request cut off by `max_output_tokens` reports itself as incomplete at the top level and as **completed** in the very item that was cut: The control, the same request with a budget it can meet, returns `"status": "completed"` with the same `"completed"` item, so the item status carries no information at all: it is the same string either way. Both item types behave this way; on a server with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, `max_output_tokens: 32` with `tool_choice: "required"` gives: (in that run the arguments happened to be complete; the point is the status, which is the same literal for a cut response as for a finished one). Go lower to look for `python3 repro_responses_item_status.py`, I pasted it in the end. `repro_responses_item_status.py` (attached; stdlib only): It asks once with `max_output_tokens: 16` and once with `400`, and exits 1 when an item says `completed` inside a response that says `incomplete` (and 2 if the control misbehaves, so a strange engine cannot be mistaken for this bug). `vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/utils.py` builds the non-harmony output items with the status as a literal: The harmony path in the same feature does it correctly, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision: So a gpt-oss/harmony deployment reports item status truthfully and every other model does not. (By claude, take it with a grain of salt, it's prob right here tho) max_output_tokens). #24184 (v0.10.1.1, closed) asked for a *top-level* signal that a Responses call hit `max_output_tokens`; that top-level `status`/`incomplete_details` now works. This report is the *per-item* `output[i].status`, a literal `"completed"` on the non-harmony path while `harmony.py` derives it from the finish reason — a distinct field, still wrong on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0. control, for both `message` and `function_call` items.

title: `/v1/messages` returns two different error envelopes. Request-validation errors come back in the OpenAI shape, with a Python repr inside the message
body: This is a simple correctness issue I believe, so I won't provide my enviroment above, should be reproducible across. The Anthropic-compatible endpoint answers errors in two different shapes depending on where the error was raised. **Raised inside the handler**, the documented Anthropic envelope: **Raised by request validation** -- the OpenAI envelope, and the message is a Python `repr`: Same endpoint, same client, two envelopes. A client written against the Anthropic API reads `body["error"]["type"]` and `body["type"] == "error"`; on a validation error neither is there. And the human-readable part is a Python dict repr, not JSON, so the detail cannot be parsed either, `'ctx': {'error': ValueError(...)}` is not machine-readable in any language. **_Reproduced on 0.27.1 and 0.29.0_** with three validation cases (`max_tokens: 0`, an unknown role, a missing `messages`); all three take the OpenAI shape on both versions. **If you want to try fix this, here is where you should look** `vllm/entrypoints/anthropic/api_router.py` has the translation and uses it for everything the handler raises: Request validation never reaches that function: FastAPI raises `RequestValidationError` before `create_messages` runs, and the app-wide validation handler answers in the OpenAI envelope for every route. `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` answer validation failures in the Anthropic envelope too, a path-scoped validation handler, or a dependency that validates and translates. `count_tokens` behaves exactly like `/v1/messages`, measured on the same 0.29.0 engine: an unknown model is a 404 in the Anthropic envelope, while a bad role and a missing `messages` field are 400s in the OpenAI one. So the fix belongs to both routes. Smaller, in the same area: even the translated errors carry the Python exception class name as `error.type` (`"NotFoundError"`), where the Anthropic API uses `not_found_error`, `invalid_request_error`, and so on -- the field SDKs switch on.

title: `echo: true` silently stops echoing when the unrelated `return_token_ids: true` is also set
body:
`echo` is the OpenAI completions field that asks the server to put the prompt back in front of the completion. vLLM's own extension `return_token_ids` asks for the engine's token ids. Set both and `echo` stops working, and there is no error, no warning, a 200 whose `text` is the completion alone: The second and third answers are the same string: with `return_token_ids` on, `echo: true` and `echo: false` are indistinguishable in the response text. `vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py` (line 270 in 0.29.0, the same line in 0.27.1): The prompt is only detokenized when `echo` is set AND `return_token_ids` is not. The reasoning is presumably "the caller can detokenize `prompt_token_ids` themselves", and the response does carry `prompt_token_ids` -- but the field the caller set is `echo`, whose documented effect is on `text`, and nothing tells them it was dropped.
repro_echo_dropped_by_return_token_ids.py, standard library only; save and run against a running server

title: `allowed_token_ids` + `bad_words` can emit tokens outside the allowlist
body: Combining two supported sampling constraints can leave no valid next token and silently break the allowlist. With Qwen3-0.6B, the text `" a"` is token 264. This request allows only token 264 and also bans `" a"`: vLLM accepts the request and returns HTTP 200, but generates token 0 four times. Token 0 is not in `allowed_token_ids`. This is not an empty `allowed_token_ids=[]` request. Both fields are non-empty, each constraint works on its own, and vLLM does not report the combination as unsupported. Applications use `allowed_token_ids` to force outputs into a fixed vocabulary, for example label IDs, routing choices, or constrained decoding. This bug can return an arbitrary out-of-domain token in a successful response, so clients that trust the allowlist can accept an invalid result without seeing an error. Start the server: Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32479783/repro_empty_sampler.py), run: The script obtains the token IDs from the model tokenizer and sends four requests: each constraint alone, the empty intersection, and a non-empty intersection control. It exits with status 1 when the out-of-allowlist result is reproduced. All four requests return HTTP 200: | Case | Constraints | Returned token IDs | Text | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Allowlist only | allow `[264]` | `[264, 264, 264, 264]` | `" a a a a"` | | Bad word only | ban token 264 | `[4710, 785, 2701, 374]` | `" \n\nThe following is"` | | Empty intersection | allow `[264]`, ban token 264 | `[0, 0, 0, 0]` | `"!!!!"` | | Non-empty control | allow `[264, 279]`, ban token 264 | `[279, 279, 279, 279]` | `" the the the the"` | The controls show that the individual processors work. Only the contradictory combination returns tokens outside the allowlist. The complete client and server output is in [server.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32479792/server_empty_sampler.log). If the active constraints leave no valid next token, vLLM should reject the request or stop

title: V1 `InputBatch` retains prompt-embedding tensors after requests finish
body: In vLLM 0.29.0's V1 model runner, a completed request can leave its `prompt_embeds` tensor referenced by `InputBatch.req_prompt_embeds`. After all requests have been removed and the persistent batch is empty, the dictionary still contains one tensor for every slot that previously handled a prompt-embedding request. Reusing those slots with ordinary token-ID requests does not release or overwrite the old tensors. They remain alive until another prompt-embedding request overwrites the same slot, the dictionary is cleared, or the worker exits. The retention is bounded by persistent-batch capacity, but a worker can keep the peak prompt-embedding footprint of a previous burst even after ordinary text requests replace that workload. The reproducer retains 256 MiB across eight reused slots and releases it only when the stale dictionary is cleared. At a `max_num_seqs` of 256, the same `(4096, 4096)` BF16 shape can retain up to 8 GiB of host memory. This can increase host-memory pressure, swapping, allocation failures, or container eviction risk. Stale entries can also cause unnecessary prompt-embedding staging work for replacement requests. Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32476544/repro_slot_retention.py), with vLLM 0.29.0 installed, run: The script reproduces a prompt-embedding burst followed by ordinary text traffic: 1. fills eight slots with `(4096, 4096)` BF16 prompt-embedding tensors, totaling 256 MiB; 2. completes all eight requests and forces garbage collection; 3. reuses every slot with an unrelated token-ID request; 4. verifies that every old tensor is still attached to the reused slot; and 5. clears only `req_prompt_embeds` as a control while the text requests remain active. The script records both weak-reference liveness and process RSS. It calls `malloc_trim()` only after clearing the dictionary so that the RSS control is visible; the weak references establish tensor lifetime independently of the allocator. The weak-reference

title: FunctionGemma rejects hyphenated tool names only in non-streaming responses
body: The `functiongemma` tool parser handles the same valid model output differently depending on whether Chat Completions is streamed. For a declared function named `get-weather`, streaming returns a structured tool call. Non-streaming returns no tool call and exposes the complete FunctionGemma control frame as assistant content: Applications can silently receive ordinary content instead of a tool call when they switch from streaming to non-streaming responses. The leaked content also contains model-specific control tokens that should have been consumed by the parser. Changing only the name to `get_weather` makes both modes work. Use the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32470722/repro_get_weather.py), with vLLM 0.29.0 installed, run: If the tokenizer is already cached, the run can be kept fully offline: The script feeds one real tokenizer token per streaming delta and compares it with a non-streaming parse of the identical output. It also runs `get_weather` as a control. Both response modes should return one structured call named `get-weather` with `{"city": "Paris"}` as its arguments and no assistant content. Hyphens are valid in OpenAI function names, and the official FunctionGemma chat template preserves the declared name in both the function declaration and assistant tool-call history. The non-streaming parser uses `\w+` for the function name: That expression stops at the hyphen, so `extract_tool_calls()` finds no match and returns the raw model output as content. The streaming path uses all text between `call:` and `{`: It therefore accepts the same name. The two paths implement different grammars for the same field. title: --kv-cache-memory suggestion double-counts CUDAGraph memory (regression of #37426, reintroduced by #49208)
body: The `--kv-cache-memory` value that vLLM prints at startup double-counts CUDA-graph memory whenever `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1` (the default). For models with a large CUDA-graph pool the suggested value comes out **negative**, so it cannot be used and, since #47374, it also silently defeats `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`. `--kv-cache-memory` (config `kv_cache_memory_bytes`) lets the operator hard-code the KV cache size in bytes. When set, vLLM skips the memory-profiling measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass, and reserves exactly that amount instead of deriving it from `--gpu-memory-utilization` (a short `profile_run()` for compilation still happens). The value is only meaningful if it reproduces the current allocation: too optimistic and the engine OOMs at graph capture, too conservative and batch concurrency (hence throughput) is capped. It is valid only on the same GPU with the same initial free memory. Because the profiled value is deterministic for a fixed (model, config, hardware, library) combination, `gpu_worker.py` recomputes the exact `--kv-cache-memory` that reproduces the current allocation on every boot and logs it at INFO (promoted from DEBUG in #47374, "Surface the --kv-cache-memory suggestion at INFO and document fast-startup knobs"). The message offers two numbers: `X` fills up to the `--gpu-memory-utilization` target; `Y` uses all free device memory. Both are meant to be copied back verbatim, and `X` is also what the opt-in `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` feature (same PR, #47374) persists under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/startup_plan/` to skip profiling on subsequent boots. That feature's guard rejects non-positive recorded values, so a negative `X` makes the whole fast-startup mechanism inert for exactly the models that would benefit most. - The copy-paste `--kv-cache-memory` suggestion is unusable (negative) on large-graph models. - `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` records the negative value and its guard rejects it, so fast startup

title: Chunked embeddings break dot-product scoring with `use_activation=true

This affects more than the reported vector norm. It changes dot-product scores, threshold decisions, and comparisons between short and long inputs. Using embeddings returned by the API, an exact long-text self-match produces a dot product of only `0.61587080`. The same vector has cosine similarity `1.0`, and its dot product becomes `1.0` after L2 normalization. For example, a dot-product threshold of `0.8` rejects an exact match: All vectors in this comparison come directly from `POST /v1/embeddings`. - vLLM: `0.29.0` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` - GPU: NVIDIA L40S - Endpoint: `POST /v1/embeddings` - Runner: pooling Pooler configuration: Start the server with `max_model_len=64` so a 128-token input is split into two chunks: Use the script: [probe_vllm_chunked_embedding_normalization.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32462928/probe_vllm_chunked_embedding_normalization.py) Run: The reproducer builds two different 64-token sequences: - `A`: repetitions of `apple orchard harvest fruit trees sunshine agriculture`; - `B`: repetitions of `quantum mechanics particle wavefunction entanglement laboratory`. It requests embeddings for: 1. `A` and `B` as ordinary 64-token inputs; 2. `A + B` as one 128-token long input; 3. the same returned vectors under representative dot-product scoring and threshold rules. Every embedding request uses: Every threshold in `(0.61587080, 1.0]` changes this decision. Every threshold in `(0.61584421, 0.78474047]` changes this decision. Using `embedding(A + B)` as the query: | Candidate | Raw dot product | Dot after normalization | |---|---:|---:| | Exact long document `A + B` | `0.61587080` | `1.00000000` | | Short half-document `A` | `0.61584421` | `0.78474047` | The exact-match margin is only `0.00002658` with the raw vLLM outputs. title: HunYuan Dense V1 fails CUDA graph capture on v0.29 — HF dynamic RoPE does a host-side sync during capture
body: - vLLM 0.29.0 (official image), 2× L40S (also reproduces TP=1), transformers 5.16 - Model: hy-mt2-7b HunYuanDenseV1ForCausalLM checkpoint, `rope_scaling = {"type": "dynamic", "alpha": 1000.0, "factor": 1.0, ...}`, `max_position_embeddings=262144` `vllm serve hy-mt2-7b --tensor-parallel-size 2` (default `cudagraph_mode=FULL`). vLLM downgrades to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (FlashAttentionBackend, UNIFORM_BATCH), then dies during capture: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py:100 `if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached:` called from modeling_hunyuan_v1_dense.py:436 `position_embeddings = self.rotary_emb(...)` Since #53615 the model runs on the Transformers backend. Dynamic-rope checkpoints go through `@dynamic_rope_update`, where `dynamic_frequency_update` does `seq_len = torch.max(position_ids) + 1; if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached:` — `Tensor.__bool__` forces a D2H sync, which is illegal inside CUDA graph capture → capture invalidated (cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated at capture_end) → startup fails. Every cudagraph mode except NONE fails (PIECEWISE capture passes 19/19 with torch.compile on, but the FULL phase / profile_cudagraph_memory still runs the raw forward and dies). Note: in vLLM `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings`, so for these checkpoints the whole dynamic update is a no-op — but the check itself still syncs. ≤0.28 native `hunyuan_v1.py` computed the NTK-alpha inv_freq statically in `__init__`; CUDA graphs worked. `--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}'` (starts, decode perf hit). - In `vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py`: bypass `dynamic_rope_update` when `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings` (update is a no-op then), or - warn + force `cudagraph_mode=NONE` for dynamic-rope models, or - (upstream transformers) make `dynamic_frequency_update` capture-safe. cc @hmellor (author of #53615)
label: bug

title: DecodeBenchConnector repeats KV cache fills for shared state tensors at large batch sizes
body: `DecodeBenchConnectorWorker.start_fill_kv()` currently processes requests one by one and fills the KV cache separately for each request. For hybrid KV cache layouts, multiple requests may reference the same state tensor. The current implementation fills the same state tensor repeatedly for every request. Block-indexed KV cache entries are also filled per request, even when block IDs overlap across requests. As the batch size increases, the repeated fill operations introduce significant overhead before the first decode step. In our vLLM-MLU testing environment, this behavior was observed during large-batch, long-context decode benchmarks and was associated with worker RPC timeouts. The repeated-fill behavior can be identified in the upstream `DecodeBenchConnector` implementation. However, the runtime timeout has so far been reproduced on the MLU backend. The issue was observed with the following configuration: - Engine: vLLM V1 - KV connector: `DecodeBenchConnector` - KV cache layout: Hybrid KV cache containing shared state tensors - Batch size: 256 - Execution backend: Multiprocessing - Workload: Long-context decode benchmark The issue occurs during the initial KV cache fill before the first decode step. Instrumentation of `start_fill_kv()` shows that shared state tensors are filled repeatedly across requests within a single invocation. As the number of requests increases, the repeated fill operations can significantly increase the initialization time. The initial KV cache fill becomes increasingly expensive at large batch sizes. In our testing environment, the excessive delay was associated with the following errors: A subsequent error while querying worker memory usage may occur after the worker RPC has already timed out. The repeated state-tensor fills occur before the first decode step. `start_fill_kv()` should avoid filling the same shared state tensor more than once within a single invocation. Block IDs should be merged and deduplicated per KV cache group befo
label: bug

title: reference detection server does not support dual_key_gumbel; detector alpha default disagrees with generation default
body: N/A — code-level report against current `main` (17e50b9b761023d5f2499f062507df1ff49092a4); no runtime environment involved. Two related gaps after #56122. `examples/basic/online_serving/watermark_detection_server.py` always constructs `GumbelWatermarkDetector` (line 60). Its argparse takes only `--tokenizer / --key / --prf / --context-width / --p-value-threshold`. There is no `--algorithm` or `--alpha`, so text generated with `algorithm="dual_key_gumbel"` cannot be detected with the reference server. `docs/features/watermarking.md` points users at this server as the deployment pattern (line 228). It should accept `--algorithm dual_key_gumbel --alpha <value>` and build `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector`. - `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector.__init__` defaults `alpha=0.2` (`vllm/v1/watermarking/gumbel.py:220`) - `WatermarkConfig.alpha` defaults to `0.1` (`vllm/config/watermarking.py:35`), as does `DualKeyGumbelWatermarker` (`gumbel.py:107`) The detector uses `alpha` in the variance normalization (`gumbel.py:252`: `variance = (1 - self.alpha) ** 2 + self.alpha ** 2`), so a silent default mismatch changes p-values. Suggest aligning the detector default to 0.1, or dropping the default and requiring `alpha` explicitly. Worth a one-line note in the constraints section that `deduplicate_contexts` and speculative decoding are mutually exclusive in effect today. It is stated at `docs/features/watermarking.md:80-82`, but under the spec-decode heading where it is easy to miss.

title: FULL_AND_PIECEWISE capture fails intermittently with cudaErrorNotPermitted when Engram PLE cpu_offload is enabled under load
